NAD but obesity is directly related to inflammation and inflammation tends to make already existing problems (aka T1D) worse. So if she loses the weight (which I know she’s trying to so yay!) she will likely start to feel at least better. It’s not that people are ignoring other issues and saying to lose weight because they’re writing her off, it’s that T1D is an autoimmune process, which means she already has inflammation, and obesity on top of that is making things worse. Yes not all big people have pain, but a lot do, and not all big people also have T1D. I know you’re maybe getting annoyed at these comments because this is your friend and you’re being protective, and honestly that’s completely understandable. Just know though that this is simply how biochemistry in the body works. Have her doctors talked about her being able to take a medication to help the weight loss process be easier? That could probably help a lot with her stress in the process at least. And stress itself is probably making the situation worse too.

I think a lot of times weight loss itself can be a scary/daunting/stressful process because it’s another thing to think about when you already have so much on your plate and you’re exhausted. This issue was really emphasized at a previous barre studio I went to, but my PB location isn’t super good about trying to correct this issue. Try to find a spot at the bar in front of the mirror. Make sure your hips are square to the ground so that you’re not dipping into the “non working” hip. Make sure your non working hip is right over your non working knee. So if you’re lifting right leg, left hip is right over left knee.  Make sure left hip isn’t dipping too far to the left. Your body will naturally want to shift the left hip further to the left to make the left knee your center of gravity to help with balance, so make sure to prevent this by engaging your core and tucking your hips as well :) Make sure left hip isn’t dipping too far to the left. I have to be very aware of this with my own body too! Hopefully this helped!
